module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 599

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/599](https://www.erdosproblems.com/599)
- [AhBe09] Aharoni, Ron and Berger, Eli, *Menger's theorem for infinite graphs*,
  *Invent. Math.* **176** (2009), 1--62.
-/

@[expose] public section

open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos599

/--
**Erdős Problem 599** (the Erdős–Menger conjecture).

Let $G$ be a (possibly infinite) graph and let $A, B$ be disjoint independent sets of
vertices. Must there exist a family $P$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint paths from $A$ to $B$,
and a set $S$ of vertices containing exactly one vertex from each path in $P$, such that
every path from $A$ to $B$ contains at least one vertex of $S$?

For finite $G$ this is equivalent to Menger's theorem. The answer is **yes**, proved by
Aharoni and Berger [AhBe09].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_599 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B : Set V),
      Disjoint A B → G.IsIndepSet A → G.IsIndepSet B →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
        (∀ i, a i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
        S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
        (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
        (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S) := by
  sorry

/--
**Menger's theorem for infinite graphs** (Aharoni–Berger [AhBe09]).

The theorem actually proved by Aharoni and Berger holds for arbitrary vertex sets $A$
and $B$: in any (possibly infinite) graph $G$ there is a family $P$ of pairwise
vertex-disjoint $A$--$B$ paths together with an $A$--$B$ separator $S$ consisting of the
choice of exactly one vertex from each path in $P$. The disjointness and independence
hypotheses of `erdos_599` are not needed.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_599.variants.aharoni_berger :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B : Set V),
      ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
        (∀ i, a i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
        S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
        (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
        (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S) := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check: when $A = \varnothing$ the conclusion of `erdos_599` holds trivially, with
the empty family of paths and $S = \varnothing$ (the covering condition is vacuous since
there is no path starting in $\varnothing$).
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_599.test.empty_A (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (B : Set V) :
    ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
      (∀ i, a i ∈ (∅ : Set V)) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
      (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
      S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
      (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
      (∀ a' ∈ (∅ : Set V), ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath →
        ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S) := by
  refine ⟨Empty, Empty.elim, Empty.elim, fun i => i.elim, ∅,
    fun i => i.elim, fun i => i.elim, fun i => i.elim, fun i => i.elim,
    fun v hv => hv.elim, fun i => i.elim, fun a' ha' => absurd ha' (Set.notMem_empty _)⟩

end Erdos599

reformulations.difference: The Lean reads "path between A and B" as any path (`IsPath` walk) from a vertex of A to a vertex of B. It uses this reading both for the family P (`p i : G.Walk (a i) (b i)`, `a i ∈ A`, `b i ∈ B`) and for the separation clause (`∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q, q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S`). Interior vertices may lie in A or B. A reader might expect Diestel-style strict A–B paths instead: paths meeting A only in the first vertex and B only in the last, with P made of such paths.
reformulations.equivalence_argument:
The two readings give the same statement.
(i) Separation. Every path from A to B contains a strict A–B sub-path: while some vertex x ≠ start lies in A, pass to `dropUntil x`; while some vertex y ≠ end lies in B, pass to `takeUntil y`. The length drops strictly each time, and the result is a strict sub-path. So "every path from A to B meets S" is equivalent to "every strict A–B path meets S".
(ii) Family. A strict witness is already a Lean witness. For the converse, take a Lean witness and let s_i be the unique S-vertex on p_i. Every sub-path of p_i from A to B meets S by separation, and it can only do so at s_i. So the same cutting procedure never removes s_i and yields a strict A–B sub-path r_i containing s_i. Replacing each p_i by r_i keeps pairwise disjointness (the supports shrink), keeps S ⊆ ⋃ supports (any v ∈ S lies on some p_i, so v = s_i ∈ r_i), keeps exactly one S-vertex per path, and keeps separation.
I proved this in Lean for arbitrary A, B in /workspace/review/strict.lean as `Scratch.concl_iff_strictConcl : Concl G A B ↔ StrictConcl G A B`, where `Concl` is the file's conclusion verbatim. `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. From it, `Scratch.rhs_iff_strict` transfers the equivalence to erdos_599's right-hand side. Aharoni–Berger's own definition is the non-strict one, which the Lean follows literally: "a finite path P is said to be an X–Y-path if in(P) ∈ X and ter(P) ∈ Y" (arXiv math/0509397, §2).

reformulations.difference: Same as for `erdos_599`, but with arbitrary A, B, which may overlap or fail to be independent. Paths from A to B may pass through other vertices of A or B. Trivial one-vertex paths at x ∈ A ∩ B are allowed, because `nil` is a path, and the separation clause then forces A ∩ B ⊆ S, as in AB09 ("S must contain X ∩ Y").
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `Scratch.concl_iff_strictConcl` is proved with no hypothesis on A and B. So the variant's body is equivalent to the version with strict A–B paths (V(P) ∩ A = {in(P)}, V(P) ∩ B = {ter(P)}) in both the family and the separator. It is also literally AB09 Theorem 1.1 with their non-strict X–Y-path definition, specialised to undirected simple graphs.

review.notes:
I checked all three declarations (`erdos_599`, `erdos_599.variants.aharoni_berger`, `erdos_599.test.empty_A`) and found no misformalization.

**The source.** erdosproblems.com/599 (read via Wayback, 2026-07-09) says: "Let G be a (possibly infinite) graph and A,B be disjoint independent sets of vertices. Must there exist a family P of disjoint paths between A and B and a set S which contains exactly one vertex from each path in P, and such that every path between A and B contains at least one vertex from S?" It is marked PROVED ("solved in the affirmative"), by Aharoni–Berger [AhBe09].

**How the Lean matches it.**
- The hypotheses match: `Disjoint A B`, `G.IsIndepSet A`, `G.IsIndepSet B`.
- Paths are finite (Lean walks), which is what AB09 requires: allowing infinite paths gives only an earlier, weaker result.
- "Disjoint" means vertex-disjoint (`Pairwise` disjoint supports), as in AB09's "warps".
- "S contains exactly one vertex from each path" is encoded as `S ⊆ ⋃ supports` plus `∃!` per path. This matches AB09's "S consists of a choice of precisely one vertex from each path in P". The looser reading, where S may contain extra vertices, would make the problem trivial (P = ∅, S = A).
- `answer(True)` elaborates to `True` (checked with `#print`), which matches "solved in the affirmative". The `research solved` category matches the source.

**Lean checks** (scratch files in /workspace/review/):
- A small positive instance (K₂, A = {0}, B = {1}) satisfies the conclusion.
- The empty family is rejected when A and B are connected, so the conclusion is not vacuous.
- The strict/non-strict path equivalence is fully proved; see the reformulations.

**Variant docstring.** It calls this "the theorem actually proved by Aharoni and Berger … in any (possibly infinite) graph G". AB09 actually prove it for digraphs. The Lean states the undirected special case, which is true and matches the docstring's "graph". I don't count this as a defect.

**Limitations.** I could not read Erdős's own wording in [Er81]/[Er87]: the Rényi PDFs are scans, and the problem was not in the extractable text. This leaves no declaration unsettled, since the cited source and the solving paper agree.

**Status.** No status issues.
